issues.legal_issue: An arbitration agreement contained in an unregistered instrument that is compulsorily registrable may remain enforceable independently of the instrument’s terms.
material_facts: The parties executed a long-term lease deed that was compulsorily registrable but had not been registered.
The deed contained an arbitration clause concerning disputes connected with the deed.
The arbitration clause was a separate agreement for resolving disputes and was not shown to be independently invalid.
issues.conclusion: The arbitration clause could be acted upon for dispute resolution despite the non-registration of the deed, subject to the exception that grounds invalidating the main agreement may also invalidate the arbitration agreement if they apply to its making.
issues.legal_principle: Registration Act, 1908, sections 17(1)(d) and 49, read with Transfer of Property Act, 1882, section 107, require registration of leases of the specified kind and restrict the use of an unregistered instrument. The proviso to section 49 permits limited uses, including evidence of a collateral transaction. An arbitration clause is an independent agreement collateral to the substantive transaction; Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, section 16(1)(a) and (b), recognises that independence. The arbitration agreement may nevertheless share the main agreement’s invalidity where the ground making the main agreement voidable also affects the making of the arbitration agreement.

rule.if: application_for_arbitrator_appointment and instrument_requires_registration and instrument_is_unregistered and arbitration_clause_is_separable and arbitration_agreement_is_not_itself_invalid

predicates.application_for_arbitrator_appointment: A party has applied for the appointment of an arbitrator under an agreement contained in an instrument.
predicates.instrument_requires_registration: The instrument records a transaction of a kind that must be registered.
predicates.instrument_is_unregistered: The instrument has not been registered.
predicates.arbitration_clause_is_separable: The instrument contains an arbitration clause that is independent of its substantive transaction terms.
predicates.arbitration_agreement_is_not_itself_inva: No ground affecting the making of the arbitration agreement makes that agreement invalid or unenforceable.

issues.definition: When an appointment application concerns an unregistered instrument that must be registered, a separable and otherwise valid arbitration clause can still be enforced for dispute resolution.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot act on an arbitration clause in an instrument chargeable with stamp duty until the instrument is duly stamped or the stamp defect is cured.
material_facts: The arbitration clause was contained in a lease deed that was alleged to be insufficiently stamped.
The court had to consider the deed in deciding the application for appointment of an arbitrator.
The stamp-duty issue had not yet been determined, so the Supreme Court remitted the matter for that determination and directed appointment of an arbitrator if the deed was duly stamped.
issues.conclusion: The court must examine whether the instrument is duly stamped and, if it is not, impound it and follow the applicable procedure; it cannot act on the instrument or its arbitration clause until the defect is cured. The matter was remitted for the stamp-duty issue to be decided first and for an arbitrator to be appointed if the instrument was duly stamped.
issues.legal_principle: Indian Stamp Act, 1899, section 33 requires examination and impounding of an instrument that appears insufficiently stamped. Section 35 bars an insufficiently stamped instrument from being admitted in evidence or acted upon, including its arbitration clause, until the duty and applicable penalty are paid. Sections 38 and 40 provide for the subsequent procedure. Unlike Registration Act, 1908, section 49, section 35 has no collateral-transaction exception.

rule.if: application_for_arbitrator_appointment and instrument_is_chargeable_with_stamp_duty and instrument_is_not_duly_stamped and stamp_defect_is_not_cured

predicates.application_for_arbitrator_appointment: A party has applied for the appointment of an arbitrator under an agreement contained in an instrument.
predicates.instrument_is_chargeable_with_stamp_duty: The instrument is of a kind on which stamp duty is payable.
predicates.instrument_is_not_duly_stamped: The instrument does not bear the stamp duty required for it.
predicates.stamp_defect_is_not_cured: The required duty and applicable penalty have not been paid.

issues.definition: When an appointment application relies on a chargeable instrument that remains insufficiently stamped, the court must impound it and cannot act on its arbitration clause until the stamp defect is cured.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitration clause does not cover a dispute arising from a separate agreement to which the clause does not apply.
material_facts: The applicant sought arbitration concerning an alleged agreement to sell the estates that predated the lease deed.
The parties had not included an arbitration agreement in the alleged sale agreement.
The arbitration clause in the lease deed covered disputes relating to or touching upon that deed.
issues.conclusion: The applicant could not seek arbitration of disputes concerning the alleged sale agreement under the arbitration clause in the lease deed.
issues.legal_principle: An arbitration agreement must be between the parties to the dispute and must relate to or apply to the dispute or its subject matter. The Court relied on Yogi Agarwal v. Inspiration Clothes & U, (2009) 1 SCC 372, which stated this principle in considering sections 7 and 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

predicates.application_for_arbitrator_appointment: A party has applied for the appointment of an arbitrator.
predicates.dispute_arises_from_separate_agreement: The dispute arises from an agreement distinct from the instrument containing the arbitration clause.
predicates.arbitration_agreement_does_not_cover_tha: The arbitration agreement does not apply to the separate agreement or the dispute arising from it.

issues.definition: A dispute arising from a separate agreement cannot be referred under an arbitration agreement that does not cover that dispute.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator cannot enforce the terms of an unregistered lease that is compulsorily registrable, and a claim outside the scope of the arbitration clause cannot be decided under that clause.
material_facts: The lease was for a term exceeding one year, was compulsorily registrable, and had not been registered.
The arbitration clause was limited to disputes relating to or touching upon the lease deed.
The applicant sought enforcement of the lease and recovery of expenditure, either as damages for failure to grant the lease or as a claim independent of the lease.
The sale-agreement dispute was not covered by the lease deed’s arbitration clause.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator could not rely on the unregistered lease to enforce its terms. If the expenditure claim was treated as damages for breach of the lease, it sought enforcement of terms that could not be relied upon; if treated as independent of the lease, it fell outside the limited arbitration clause.
issues.legal_principle: Registration Act, 1908, sections 17 and 49, and Transfer of Property Act, 1882, sections 106 and 107, govern registration and the effect of non-registration of the lease. An unregistered instrument cannot affect the immovable property or be received as evidence of a transaction affecting it, subject to the limited uses in section 49. An arbitrator may not rely on the instrument to enforce its lease terms. A claim must also fall within the scope of the arbitration agreement, as reflected in the principle stated in Yogi Agarwal v. Inspiration Clothes & U, (2009) 1 SCC 372.

rule.if: arbitration_proceeding_concerns_lease and lease_requires_registration and lease_is_unregistered and arbitration_clause_is_limited_to_lease_disputes and (claim_seeks_enforcement_of_lease_terms or claim_is_outside_clause_scope)

predicates.arbitration_proceeding_concerns_lease: The arbitration proceeding concerns a lease.
predicates.lease_requires_registration: The lease is of a kind that must be registered.
predicates.lease_is_unregistered: The lease has not been registered.
predicates.arbitration_clause_is_limited_to_lease_d: The arbitration clause covers only disputes relating to or touching upon the lease.
predicates.claim_seeks_enforcement_of_lease_terms: The claim requires relying on the lease to enforce its terms or obtain damages for their breach.
predicates.claim_is_outside_clause_scope: The claim is framed independently of the lease and is not covered by the arbitration clause.

issues.definition: When an arbitration clause is limited to lease disputes, an arbitrator cannot decide a claim that requires enforcing an unregistered lease or a claim that falls outside the clause’s scope.
